title: と — “and” (nouns) and “with”
summary: と has two basic uses for beginners: it joins nouns like ‘and’ (パンと牛乳), and it marks a partner with whom you do something, like ‘with’ (母と行く). It attaches to nouns. It has other uses too (quoting, ‘if’), learned later.

patterns.gloss: noun A and noun B (complete list)
person + と + verb: do something with that person

body.p: A と B lists exactly the things named: パンと牛乳を買いました (bread and milk). It only connects nouns, not verbs or adjectives. For ‘and so on’, use や instead.
Put と after the person you do something with: 母と買い物に行きます (I go shopping with my mother). To say you do it alone, use ひとりで. A partner must be someone who also takes part.
と also marks quotations (～と言う) and conditions (春になると…). You will study these later; in this lesson focus on the two uses above.

examples.ja: 私（わたし）と友達（ともだち）は公園（こうえん）へ行（い）きました。
examples.romaji: Watashi to tomodachi wa kōen e ikimashita.
examples.tr: My friend and I went to the park.
examples.note: と joins the two subjects, 私 and 友達.

examples.ja: パンと牛乳（ぎゅうにゅう）を買（か）いました。
母（はは）と買（か）い物（もの）に行（い）きます。
examples.tr: I go shopping with my mother.
examples.note: と marks the person who goes together.

pitfalls: と joins nouns only. To link verbs or adjectives, use the て-form instead.
と means a complete list. For examples among several, use や: パンや牛乳を買いました.
